title: Video passthrough latency, fidelity, and distortion in AR headsets
bottleneck: Video see-through headsets reconstruct the world from cameras, but the pipeline adds latency, geometric distortion, limited dynamic range, and resolution loss versus natural vision. Even tens of milliseconds of photon-to-photon delay and subtle warping break hand-eye coordination and cause discomfort, and no shipping headset matches the naked eye.
why_it_blocks: Passthrough quality is the ceiling on mixed reality's core promise: blending virtual content with the real world. Until the reconstruction is perceptually transparent, professional and all-day use cases stay out of reach, and the device remains a compromise rather than a replacement for clear optics.
current_state: Flagship headsets keep improving sensor arrays and reprojection algorithms, but teardowns document persistent artifacts: motion blur, low-light noise, and distortion at frame edges. The gap between passthrough and reality is narrowing incrementally, not closing.
